module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 17

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section


namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture17

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 17](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, the size `b(G)` of a largest induced bipartite subgraph
satisfies `b(G) ≥ α(G) + ⌈diam(G) / 3⌉`, where `α(G)` is the independence number of `G`
and `diam(G)` is the diameter of `G`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture17 (G : SimpleGraph α) (h : G.Connected) :
    (G.indepNum : ℝ) + ⌈(G.diam : ℝ) / 3⌉ ≤ b G := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The invariant `b G` is nonneg (it's the cast of a natural number). -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ b G := Nat.cast_nonneg _

/-- The independence number `α(K₂)` equals 1 (each independent set contains at most one vertex). -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).edgeFinset.card = 1 := by decide

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture17

findings.description: Lines 54–56 hold the second sanity-check `example` (it has no name). Its docstring reads "The independence number `α(K₂)` equals 1 (each independent set contains at most one vertex)." Its Lean statement is `(⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).edgeFinset.card = 1`, which counts the edges of K₂ and never mentions `indepNum`. So the docstring describes a different claim from the one checked: both numbers happen to be 1, but this test does not exercise the independence number the conjecture uses. The main theorem `conjecture17` is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: This is not a source question. The mismatch is inside FormalConjectures/WrittenOnTheWallII/GraphConjecture17.lean, lines 54–56: the docstring says "The independence number `α(K₂)` equals 1", while the Lean is `example : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).edgeFinset.card = 1 := by decide`.
findings.suggested_fix: Test what the docstring says: `example : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).indepNum = 1 := by rw [indep_num_eq_computable]; decide`. I checked that this compiles at this commit with `open SimpleGraph`. Alternatively, change the docstring to "`K₂` has exactly one edge."

reformulations.difference: The Lean adds the hypothesis `[Nontrivial α]` (at least two vertices), which the source does not have: it speaks of every simple connected graph, including the one-vertex graph K₁. The inequality is also stated in ℝ, with `Int.ceil` of the real quotient `diam/3` cast back to ℝ. That part is cosmetic.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: `G.Connected` already implies `Nonempty α`, so the only connected graph that `[Nontrivial α]` excludes is the one-vertex graph. The inequality holds there. First, diam = 0 (`diam_eq_zero_of_subsingleton`). Second, α(G) ≤ b(G) for every finite graph, since a maximum independent set induces an edgeless, hence 2-colourable, subgraph. So α + ⌈0/3⌉ = 1 ≤ 1 = b(K₁). In a scratch file I proved `indepNum_le_b`, the one-vertex case `subsingleton_case`, and the ↔ between the statement with and without `[Nontrivial α]` (for α : Type), using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

sources_consulted: http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/ (live page: redirects to https, which timed out)
review.notes:
What the source says. The live WOWII site timed out, so I read the Wayback Machine snapshots from November 2021; the menu says the page was last updated 4/08/20. The entry reads: "T 17. If G is a simple connected graph, then b(G) ≥ α(G) + CEIL(diam(G)/3)". Its definitions link is printDefinitions(15,5,14,16), which resolves to:
- b(G): "The maximum number of vertices of an induced bipartite subgraph of the graph"
- α(G): "The maximum number of vertices such that no two are adjacent"
- diam(G): "The maximum of eccentricities of vertices of the graph"
- CEIL[x]: "The smallest integer greater than or equal to x"
The remark says: "July 3, 2003. Independently proven by Benny John, UHD (Dec. 2005) and David Schindl, Gerard Univ (Jan. 2006)." `resolved.htm` also lists #17 as T.

What the Lean says. `#print` shows the statement elaborates to `↑α(G) + ↑⌈↑G.diam / 3⌉ ≤ G.b`, with the real division taken before the ceiling. This is the source's inequality, with the same direction and the same invariants:
- `indepNum` is Mathlib's independence number.
- `diam` is `ediam.toNat`, which is the true diameter for a connected finite graph.
- `b` is the sSup of card s over the s with `(G.induce s).IsBipartite`; the set is bounded and nonempty on a Fintype.

Status. The `research solved` tag matches the source's T, so there is no status issue.

Checks I ran:
- The computable versions give the expected values: b(K₃)=2, α(K₃)=1, b(C₅)=4, α(C₅)=2, b(P₄)=4, α(P₄)=2.
- A brute-force check over all connected labelled graphs on 2–6 vertices (1, 4, 38, 728 and 26,704 of them, matching OEIS A001187) found no violation of b ≥ α + ⌈diam/3⌉. This is consistent with the theorem being proved and with the formal statement not being trivially false.
- The hypotheses can be satisfied (for example by K₂), so the statement is not vacuous.

No misformalization of the main theorem was found. The only finding is the minor docstring/Lean mismatch in the second test example.
